In an interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and the company's vision for a tabless interface. Watch the video below.

ChatGPT may seamlessly integrate work functionality

A few days ago, Joanna Stern posted a teaser of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern released the full interview, covering topics including new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware plans, the Apple lawsuit, and the recent Hugging Face hack.

During the interview, Stern discussed OpenAI's recent decision to merge ChatGPT with the Codex desktop app while simultaneously launching a brand-new ChatGPT agent mode called "Work."

The merged interface caused significant confusion among users, particularly those who simply wanted to continue using ChatGPT but couldn't find their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, adding separate "Work" and "Chat" tabs at the top of the interface and a dropdown menu in the left panel for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. While navigation became somewhat easier, the overall experience remains complex.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's description of the new interface as "a bit of a mess" and added that this represents "incremental progress" toward the future, where the "Work" tab will eventually disappear and its functionality will be "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also noted that despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI achieved the desired effect, with Codex users doubling from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether this growth was simply a result of shoving Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman conceded again, while also arguing that this was always part of the plan:

The full interview is fascinating and well worth watching. It also features a very "Joanna Stern" segment where she attempts to incorporate ChatGPT's voice feature into the conversation, which goes about as smoothly as you'd expect.
